title: Disney strikes $20-million deal for Character.ai's assets as AI startup files for bankruptcy
source_used: Los Angeles Times (own reporting, full text read)
key_facts: Character.ai, a Menlo Park, California startup, filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy (LA Times).

Its app lets people create and chat with bots that mimic celebrities, historical figures or other characters; it reached a $1 billion valuation in 2023 and has more than 20 million monthly active users.

Character.ai said that before filing it struck an agreement under which Disney would pay $20 million to license certain intellectual property from the startup (the article's body says license; the headline says assets).
In a blog post late Monday (12 Oct) the company said the bankruptcy will help it move to a court-supervised sale by the end of this year; if no workable bid comes, the platform will be wound down.
The platform continues to run as usual during the sale, according to the company.

Parents in several states sued, alleging chatbots harmed their children; earlier this year Character.ai and Google agreed to settle several of those suits (Colorado, Florida, Texas, New York). The company says it takes safety seriously and has put limits on minors.
Last year it removed chatbots impersonating Disney characters such as Elsa and Darth Vader after a Disney cease-and-desist letter.
Former CEO Karandeep Anand, ex-Facebook, left this year to become Disney's first chief technology officer; Colin Adams is CEO now.
quote_evidence: Character.ai said before the bankruptcy filing it struck an agreement with Disney in which the entertainment company agreed to pay $20 million to license certain intellectual property from the AI startup.

why_it_matters_hint: A chatbot app used by over 20 million people monthly is in bankruptcy after lawsuits over harm to young users, and may be sold or shut down.

notes: The Disney payment is Character.ai's own account in the article; Disney is not quoted. Earlier Reuters-based coverage in our 9 Oct edition covered a Kentucky attorney general lawsuit against Character.AI.
